models_evaluated: NLP algorithm for identifying injuries associated with child physical abuse

links.outcome: Whether silent-mode running on live ED notes enabled algorithm refinement before clinical activation
links.effect: 73 of 353 notes falsely triggered the NLP, mostly from linguistic-context errors. Common false-positive scenarios were identified and the algorithm was refined to improve specificity.
links.quote: Analysis of an NLP algorithm in "silent mode" allowed for refinement of the algorithm and highlighted areas in which real-time CDS may help ED providers identify and pursue appropriate evaluation of injuries associated with child physical abuse.

links.outcome: Silent-mode NLP outputs compared with actual clinician evaluation and guideline adherence on live notes
links.effect: Adherence to guideline-recommended evaluation was 63%. Seventy-three false triggers were found and used to refine the algorithm.
links.quote: Seventy-three cases falsely triggered the NLP, often due to errors in interpreting linguistic context.

unlisted_practices: Using NLP surveillance results to identify where real-time clinical decision support could improve child abuse evaluation

screen.reason: Evaluates the implementation of an NLP clinical decision support algorithm run in 'silent mode' across multiple emergency departments to refine triggers and detect guideline adherence and disparities before active deployment.
